review: 1:1 כְּרוּעוּ — 'bow down', the imperative of כָּרַע used in Ps 95:6; the Arabic اسْجُدُوا is the same posture, but כָּרַע fits the 9-syllable line where הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ would not.

1:3–1:4 וְהַגְדִּילוּהוּ כִּי הוּא / הַמּוֹשִׁיעַ הַיָּחִיד — the Arabic splits 'the Only Savior' across the line break (الـ / ـمُخَلِّصُ); Hebrew cannot split the word, so the whole phrase sits on 1:4.
2:2 מָתוֹק נִשָּׂא — 'sweet, exalted'; the Arabic حُلْوٌ سَامٍ is two adjectives on one noun (name), and Hebrew carries both on the implied שֵׁם.

3:4 תַּם הַכֹּל בַּצְּלָב — 'all is finished on the cross'; the Arabic quotes «تَمَّ» (John 19:30). The Greek τετέλεσται is rendered in Hebrew tradition by נִשְׁלַם, but תַּם is the biblical verb (Lam 4:22) and keeps the line at six.
